hypothesis-test.context: Two overlapping bell curves separated by a dashed cutoff line. Used for significance testing, p values and comparing a null result with an alternative in statistics reports.

forest-plot.context: Rows of small squares with horizontal whiskers crossing a vertical reference line. Used in meta analysis and medical research to show effect sizes with confidence intervals.

mean-x-bar.context: The letter x with a bar above it, the symbol for a sample mean. Used in statistics tools, formulas and calculators that report an average.

probability-tree.context: A tree diagram that branches twice from a single point, showing possible outcomes. Used in probability lessons, decision analysis and risk calculations.

outlier-point.context: A scatter plot where one lone point sits far from the cluster and is circled. Used to flag anomalies, unusual values and data quality problems.

data-sampling.context: A large circle of dots with a smaller circle holding a sample taken from it. Used for sampling methods, survey design and working with subsets of a population.

satisfaction-gauge.context: A half round gauge with its needle turned toward the high end and a smile below it. Used for customer satisfaction scores, happiness surveys and service ratings.

rating-distribution.context: A star beside five bars that get shorter row by row. Used on review pages and dashboards to show how many ratings each star level received.

uptime-bars.context: A row of status bars where two short bars mark periods of downtime. Used on status pages and monitoring tools to show service availability over time.

tally-marks.context: Four upright strokes crossed by a fifth, with two more strokes beside them. Used for counting by hand, scoring games and simple frequency counts.

tally-stick.context: A wooden stick with a row of counting notches cut into its edge. Used for early record keeping, historical accounting and counting topics.

quipu.context: A main cord with several knotted cords hanging from it. The Andean quipu recorded numbers and records with knots; used in history, museum and counting topics.

census.context: A clipboard form showing a house and a tick line. Used for population censuses, household surveys and government data collection.

demographics.context: Three people of different sizes above a pie chart. Used for audience breakdowns, population statistics and reports on age, gender or location groups.

market-research.context: A magnifying glass held over a person. Used for customer research, market studies, user interviews and audience insight.

audience-segments.context: A circle split into three separate segments, each holding a person. Used for customer segmentation, targeting and grouping users into cohorts.

customer-churn.context: A person inside an open ring with an arrow leaving through the gap. Used for churn rate, cancelled subscriptions and lost customer reports.

retention-curve.context: Axes with a curve that drops steeply and then levels off, beside a person marker. Used for user retention, cohort analysis and survival charts.

user-journey.context: A dotted winding path leading from a person to a finish flag. Used for customer journey maps, onboarding flows and user experience planning.

user-flow.context: One screen linked by arrows to two further screens. Used for user flow diagrams, wireframes and planning how people move through an app.

click-heatmap.context: A web page with heat rings around a clicked spot and a mouse pointer. Used for click maps, heatmap tools and understanding where visitors click.

scroll-depth.context: A tall page with a dashed line and an arrow showing how far down a visitor scrolled. Used for scroll tracking and measuring how much of a page is read.

session-recording.context: A browser window with a dotted pointer trail and a play button. Used for session replay tools that play back how a visitor moved through a site.

bounce-rate.context: An arrow that hits a web page and bounces straight back out. Used for bounce rate metrics and visitors who leave after one page.

click-through-rate.context: A mouse pointer clicking a link bar with a percent sign beside it. Used for click through rate in ads, email campaigns and search results.

page-views.context: A web page window with an eye in its centre. Used for page view counts, traffic statistics and visit reports.

impressions.context: An eye above three rising bars. Used for ad impressions, reach and view counts in marketing and social media reports.

web-analytics.context: A browser window holding a small bar chart. Used for website statistics, traffic dashboards and site performance reports.

mobile-analytics.context: A smartphone with a bar chart on its screen. Used for app analytics, mobile usage statistics and phone dashboards.

location-analytics.context: A map pin beside a small bar chart. Used for location data, store visits, regional sales and foot traffic reports.

ab-testing.context: Two panels marked A and B with a tick under the winning one. Used for split tests, experiments and comparing two versions of a page or feature.

okr.context: A target hit in the centre beside a short list of key results. Used for objectives and key results, goal setting and quarterly planning.

scenario-analysis.context: A line that splits into three dashed paths going up, straight and down. Used for best case, base case and worst case forecasts and what if planning.

monte-carlo-simulation.context: Several random paths fanning out from one starting point. Used for Monte Carlo simulations, risk models and probabilistic forecasts.

swot-matrix.context: A two by two grid holding the letters S, W, O and T. Used for SWOT analysis of strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats in strategy work.

risk-matrix.context: A three by three grid with the top right cell filled and nearby cells marked. Used for risk assessments that rate likelihood against impact.

chart-cycle-diagram.context: Four curved arrows chasing each other round a circle. Used for cycle diagrams, repeating processes and continuous improvement loops.

infographic.context: A tall page with a pie chart, text lines and a row of bars. Used for infographics, visual summaries and data stories.

annual-report.context: A bound report with a bar chart on its cover and a ribbon bookmark. Used for yearly company reports, financial results and investor documents.

live-data.context: A pulse line that ends in a dot sending out broadcast arcs. Used for real time data, streaming feeds and live monitoring.

monitoring-wall.context: A wall of four screens on a stand, each showing a small chart. Used for control rooms, network operations centres and dashboard displays.

metadata.context: A document with a label tag tied to it by a string. Used for file properties, metadata fields, tagging and attributes.

array-data.context: A row of adjoining cells with an index mark under each one. Used for arrays, lists and indexed data structures in programming.

directed-graph.context: Four nodes joined by one way arrows. Used for directed graphs, dependencies, workflows and network diagrams.

ring-buffer.context: A ring split into segments with some filled and a pointer at the next write position. Used for circular buffers, queues and streaming memory.

olap-cube.context: A cube divided into smaller blocks on each face. Used for OLAP cubes, multidimensional data and slice and dice analysis.

data-warehouse.context: A warehouse building with a database cylinder in its doorway. Used for data warehouses, central analytics stores and enterprise data platforms.

data-silo.context: A tall farm silo with a domed top, banded like stacked database discs. Used to describe isolated, departmental data that is not shared.

graph-database.context: A database cylinder with a small graph of linked nodes on its side. Used for graph databases, knowledge graphs and relationship data.

data-entry.context: A form sheet being filled in above a keyboard. Used for data entry work, typing records and manual input.

data-snapshot.context: A database cylinder framed by camera viewfinder corners. Used for database snapshots, point in time copies and backups.

data-collection.context: A clipboard checklist with data dots dropping in from above. Used for gathering data, surveys, field research and questionnaires.

data-split.context: One table dividing into a larger and a smaller table. Used for splitting datasets into training and test sets and partitioning data.

missing-data.context: A table with one cell drawn dashed and holding a question mark. Used for missing values, nulls, gaps and data quality checks.

pivot-table.context: A table with a header row and column and a two way arrow at its corner. Used for pivot tables, cross tabs and summarizing spreadsheet data.

freeze-panes.context: A spreadsheet with its top row and first column filled in as locked, plus a snowflake. Used for freezing header rows and columns while scrolling.

merge-cells.context: One wide cell with arrows pointing in from both sides. Used for merging table cells into one and combining columns.

split-cells.context: A wide cell divided by a new line with arrows pointing outward. Used for splitting a merged cell into separate cells.

conditional-formatting.context: A column of table cells holding data bars of different lengths. Used for conditional formatting rules, data bars and colour scales in spreadsheets.

table-row.context: A table grid with one full row filled in. Used for selecting, inserting or marking a table row or a single record.

table-column.context: A table grid with one full column filled in. Used for selecting, inserting or marking a column or field.

transpose-table.context: A tall one column table and a wide one row table with a curved arrow between them. Used for transposing data by swapping rows and columns.

spreadsheet-cell.context: A grid with one selected cell framed in bold and a small fill handle at its corner. Used for active cells, cell selection and autofill in spreadsheets.

workbook-tabs.context: A spreadsheet grid above a row of sheet tabs, the first one active. Used for workbooks, worksheet tabs and switching between sheets.

sort-alphabetical.context: The letters A over Z beside a downward arrow. Used for sorting lists by name from A to Z.

sort-numeric.context: The numbers 1 over 9 beside a downward arrow. Used for sorting lists by number from lowest to highest.

data-flow-diagram.context: A source box, a process circle and an open ended data store joined by arrows. Used for data flow diagrams in system analysis and design.

etl-process.context: Source and target database cylinders with a gear and an arrow between them. Used for extract, transform and load jobs and data pipelines.

data-integration.context: Lines from two small databases merging into one larger database. Used for combining data sources into a single system.

data-migration.context: An arrow arching from one database cylinder over to another. Used for moving data between systems, database migrations and transfers.

data-sync.context: Two database cylinders joined by arrows running in both directions. Used for data synchronization, replication and two way sync.

data-aggregation.context: Several small points joined by lines into one larger point. Used for aggregating data, roll ups, summaries and group by operations.

data-ingestion.context: A wide funnel over a database with data dots dropping into it. Used for ingesting data into storage, import jobs and intake pipelines.

data-hub.context: A database cylinder in the centre with spokes to four nodes. Used for central data hubs, hub and spoke integration and shared data platforms.

data-mesh.context: A grid of small blocks, each linked to its neighbours. Used for data mesh architecture, domain owned data and decentralised platforms.

batch-processing.context: A stack of three boxes with an arrow feeding them into a gear. Used for batch jobs, bulk processing and scheduled data runs.
